intro: Rybakina dethroned Sabalenka at the US Open this week, claiming both the title and the No. 1 ranking in one ruthless sweep. That's your biggest story — let's get into the rest.

stories.headline: Rybakina Ends Sabalenka's Reign, Grabs No. 1 and a US Open Crown in One Shot
stories.body: Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win her first US Open title and her third Grand Slam, ending Sabalenka's 99-week run at world No. 1 in the process. Becoming the first Kazakh woman to hold the top ranking is a nice bonus; denying Sabalenka a third straight title here probably feels even better.

stories.headline: Zverev Wins the US Open at a Reasonable Hour; Shelton's Night Was Less Civilized
stories.body: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 to claim the US Open and his second Grand Slam title of 2026, while Shelton still walks away ranked No. 4 in the world after a run that included eliminating Carlos Alcaraz in a match that ended at 3:33 a.m. — the latest finish in US Open history. Shelton lost the final, but his schedule was arguably the tougher draw.

stories.headline: Your Updated ATP Top Four: Sinner, Zverev, Alcaraz, and the Guy Who Kept Them All Up Past Midnight
stories.body: Post-US Open ATP rankings have Jannik Sinner at No. 1, Zverev at No. 2, Alcaraz at No. 3, and Shelton jumping to No. 4 off his finalist run. Alcaraz is ranked above the man who beat him at 3:33 in the morning, which feels like the least he deserves.
